design_reference: Concept B (upper-right granite egg) from the 2x2 incubation pod scratch-pad in this conversation.

outputs.role: Main open horizontal egg body only
outputs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: single-object image-to-3D reference, first of TWO SEPARATE MATCHING ASSETS.
Use ONLY concept B (upper-right pale granite egg) in the supplied concept sheet as the design reference. Generate one new full-frame image of the MAIN OPEN EGG BODY ALONE. No contact sheet or panels. Do not include the detached hatch, fragments, extra props or a human.

Preserve B's weathered pale-grey granite shell, smooth warm-grey mineral cavity, understated branching fossil-like alien metal/ceramic inlays in its interior, and sparse almost colourless transparent nutritional jelly residue at the lowest interior surfaces. This is an ancient alien human-clone incubation vessel that looks primarily like a natural stone egg. It has just hatched and is empty; most of its jelly was consumed during growth.

Requested changes:
1. Lay the whole egg HORIZONTALLY, resting naturally on its long curved side. Its longitudinal axis runs left to right, tapered nose at LEFT, broad rounded rear at RIGHT. Recognizable natural egg geometry, approximately 2.2 m long and 1.3 m broad when closed, enough for a curled young adult. No stand or cradle.
2. Atmospheric-entry scorching concentrated on the LEFT tapered nose: blackened and dark-brown heat damage, slightly glassy/vitrified stone grains and small ablation pits, fading gradually into the original pale granite with modest rearward heat streaks. This is cooled old surface damage, not glowing lava, flames or smoke.
3. Replace the jagged fractured opening with ONE deliberate, smooth-edged, elongated oval hatch opening in the upper near side. The absent hatch is a single shallow convex fitted stone panel, flush with the original egg surface when closed. The opening has a continuous subtly recessed dark ceramic-metal sealing lip and smoothly finished stone edges, not sharp broken chips. Preserve substantial shell thickness and enough of the upper far side and both ends that the original egg silhouette is legible. The opening follows the egg's long axis, narrower toward the nose, rounded toward the rear, about 65% of the pod length and 55% of its breadth. It exposes the hollow interior. The hatch itself MUST NOT be shown anywhere in this image.
4. Alien technology stays discreet and embedded in rock; no screens, tubing, machine chassis, riveted spacecraft plating or sci-fi glow.

Composition: one isolated complete body centered with ample margin, three-quarter perspective from above and the near side so the entire open cavity and scorched nose are clearly visible. Long side mostly broadside; gentle perspective. Plain white studio background, soft neutral illumination and restrained grounding shadow. Photoreal game-prop material study with clean readable solid geometry for image-to-3D. Opaque rough granite outside, smooth lining inside, very small clear jelly remnants; no filling pool. No text, labels, measurements, arrows, human, fetus, creature, plants, ground terrain, detached pieces or second view.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: single-object image-to-3D reference, second of TWO SEPARATE MATCHING ASSETS.
The supplied image is a DESIGN REFERENCE for the already approved horizontal open granite incubation egg. Generate ONLY ITS DETACHED HATCH, as one isolated component. DO NOT render the egg body or its cavity, even in the background. Do not render a closed egg, another pod, a tray, extra pieces, inset views or multiple panels.

The object is the single smooth fitted stone hatch that exactly belongs to the elongated oval aperture visible in the supplied pod. Its perimeter is a long organic oval, slightly narrower/pointed at the LEFT nose end and broader/rounded at the RIGHT rear end, matching the reference's opening. It is a SHALLOW CONVEX SHELL PANEL, NOT an entire egg: roughly 1.4 metres long and 0.75 metres wide, 5-8 cm thick at the edge, with a gentle outward rise that would complete the egg's missing curved exterior. Its long axis lies horizontally left to right. All edges smoothly finished, continuous and deliberate, no broken or jagged fracture. No hinge, handle, bolt or projecting latch.

Show the OUTER CONVEX FACE as the dominant visible surface in a three-quarter view slightly from above and the near side, with enough exposed edge to read the smooth shell thickness and continuous slim dark ceramic-metal sealing/mating rim underneath. The exterior matches the reference pod precisely: pale grey/tan granite with coarse black, white and warm mineral grains, gently worn rather than polished countertop. The stone forms one continuous, uncluttered curved surface; no visible window or hole. A modest dark-brown-to-charcoal heat stain on the narrow LEFT end fades into untouched pale stone; much less scorching than the pod's deeply blackened nose, as this hatch sits behind its tip. No orange glow or flames. Very subtle ancient nonhuman engineering integrated into the narrow sealing edge only, same muted dark bronze/ceramic material as the reference interior. The smooth rim should make it clearly a deliberately released hatch rather than a rock shard.

Rest this single detached panel naturally on its edge/underside, OUTER SURFACE upward toward the camera, long side horizontal, without a stand. White studio background, soft neutral lighting matching the supplied image, small grounding shadow. Entire object visible, centered with ample clear margin and readable silhouette, photorealistic game-prop reference for reconstructing a separate solid 3D asset. No text, labels, rulers, people, background environment, egg body or other objects.
